in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, this would include:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course at a university or college that isn't a higher education course (i.e., not a degree)

Or has he perhaps left education/training recently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education, so Alex would still be eligible based on his education status.

Now I just need to check a few more things:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's focused on his studies. And he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

✅ **You live in the UK**
✅ **Alex lives with you** – meaning you're responsible for him
✅ **Alex is in approved education** – A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education
✅ **Alex is under 20** – Child Benefit can continue until age 20 if the child stays in approved education or training
✅ **Alex is not working 24+ hours per week** and is not receiving benefits in his own right
✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex**

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you'll need to submit an application to HMRC.

Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
